title: Who Are the RUF/NEKS? OU's Spirit Squad and Its 1915 Roots
question: Who are the RUF/NEKS at Oklahoma and how did they get their name?
answer: The RUF/NEKS are OU's all-male spirit squad, founded in 1915 and billed as the oldest male spirit group in college sports. The name comes from "roughnecks," an insult a fan hurled at the noisy students that they adopted with pride.
summary: The RUF/NEKS, OU's all-male spirit squad, date to 1915 and took their name from a fan who called them roughnecks. They drive the Sooner Schooner today.
body: If you have watched the Sooner Schooner race across Owen Field, you have watched the RUF/NEKS at work. The all-male spirit squad was founded in 1915 and claims to be the oldest male spirit group in college sports. Its centennial was celebrated in 2015 with a reunion that drew members going back to the 1960s.

The name has a fun origin story. During a basketball game, an elderly female fan grew tired of the racket a group of male students was making and called them roughnecks. Rather than take offense, the students took it as a compliment and ran with it. The term also nods to Oklahoma's oil field workers, the hard-working roughnecks of the state's economy.

By 1921 the group had started carrying its signature red and white paddles, and members have long beaten them on the ground as they run across the field. Over the years the RUF/NEKS became a game-day fixture, firing shotguns in pregame festivities and after OU scores, and caring for the Big Red Rocket, a 1923 Model T.

Their most visible job came with the Schooner. A freshman RUF/NEK, Mick Cottom, drove the wagon in its 1964 debut, and today the RUF/NEKS and the RUF/NEK Lil' Sis maintain and drive it after Oklahoma scores. The group also keeps lighter traditions, from an annual beard-growing contest to service projects such as hiding Easter eggs for students at the Jane Brooks School for the Deaf in Chickasha.
